# GPU execution {#sec-ch12}

Every kintera call that does heavy work runs on the device of its input tensors. The same function call computes on
the CPU when the tensors live in host memory and on an NVIDIA GPU when they live in CUDA memory. This chapter
explains how one call reaches the right code, how the CUDA kernels lay out their work, how much memory each GPU
thread needs, how to build the CUDA library, and how far CPU and CUDA results agree.

The five schemes depend on each other in one direction: the build (@sec-ch12-build) enables the CUDA kernels;
dispatch (@sec-ch12-dispatch) selects them from the inputs' device; the element loops and their workspaces
(@sec-ch12-kernels) run the per-cell solvers that dispatch chose; and the device function tables
(@sec-ch12-device-functions) and the sparse solver (@sec-ch12-sparse-solver) are CUDA back ends of schemes derived
in other chapters. What the CPU and CUDA sides must share, and what `check_ch12_twins.py` checks statically at the
code pin, is listed in @sec-ch12-dispatch, Tests.

| @sec-ch12-device-functions | always on CUDA | on CUDA | `test_reaction_equilibrium.py` |
| @sec-ch12-sparse-solver | always on CUDA | on CUDA | `test_atm2d.py` |
